purpose: Decide, from the measured study in phase10_conformal.json, what interval each model should report. The rule is fixed here before looking at which model benefits, so the choice cannot be made per-model to flatter a number.
preSpecifiedRule: A method is adopted only if its measured held-out coverage is at least the nominal level minus 0.02.
Among methods that pass, the narrowest mean interval width wins.
If no method reaches nominal, the model reports the achieved coverage explicitly and the interval must not be described as a 90% interval.
Group-level intervals are preferred for any model whose rows are repeated measures within a biological unit, because that is the unit a prediction is about.
No interval may be tuned on the same held-out groups it is scored on.

mizuna-microbial-relative-load-v2.reason: Every row-level method sits at 0.86-0.87 against a nominal 0.90, and adding methods does not move it: the failure is the exchangeability unit, not the quantile. Rows are tissues within a pillow, so a row-level interval was answering the wrong question. The group-level interval reaches 0.992 at 3.40 SD of within-campaign load, which is wider but is the interval the claim actually needs.
mizuna-microbial-relative-load-v2.reportedAs: 90% group-level interval, calibrated on held-out pillows
mizuna-microbial-relative-load-v2.honestCaveat: 0.992 is the measured coverage across 35 pillows in two campaigns. Two campaigns are not a sample of campaigns; a third campaign's offset must come from its own baseline samples.

mizuna-microbial-load-v1.reason: Same diagnosis. Row-level CV+ reaches only 0.886; the group-level interval reaches 0.992 at 7.26 log10 CFU/g. This model's cross-campaign transfer already fails, so a wide, honest interval is the correct output rather than a narrow, wrong one.
mizuna-microbial-load-v1.reportedAs: 90% group-level interval, calibrated on held-out pillows
mizuna-microbial-load-v1.honestCaveat: Coverage within the two observed campaigns. The model still does not transfer to an unseen campaign's absolute level.

lettuce-earth-growth-v2.reason: CV+ beats the shipped split method on both criteria at once: coverage 0.961 against 0.907, and a narrower interval (329 g against 475 g). No trade-off to argue about. Group-level is not used here because the four experiments are far apart in level and a group-maximal interval inflates to 1023 g, which is useless as a per-plant interval.
lettuce-earth-growth-v2.reportedAs: 90% cross-conformal interval, calibrated on held-out experiments
lettuce-earth-growth-v2.honestCaveat: Four experiments. Coverage of 0.961 is over-covered and over-fitted to those four; treat the interval as descriptive of this dataset's spread.

lettuce-earth-growth-v1.reason: Same treatment as v2 so no served model states a coverage it has not measured. CV+ reaches 0.939 against split's 0.908 and is narrower (347 g against 583 g).
lettuce-earth-growth-v1.reportedAs: 90% cross-conformal interval, calibrated on held-out experiments
lettuce-earth-growth-v1.honestCaveat: Four experiments. The interval describes this dataset's spread; it is not a guarantee for a new greenhouse.

rejected.split: The Phase 9 method. Under-covers on every model that had a nominal target (0.870, 0.886, 0.908, 0.907).
rejected.mondrian: Identical to cv_plus on the microbial tasks because the campaign strata are too small to carry their own 90% quantile, so it adds a named method without adding a distinct estimate. Not adopted where it duplicates rather than improves.
rejected.inflateRadius: Deliberately not done. Widening a radius until it hits 0.90 on the evaluation groups is tuning on the test set. Group-level conformal reaches nominal for a principled reason; inflation would reach it by cheating.
